The Petitioners have filed this petition against Respondents for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989.

2. The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 21.08.2022 at about 3.55 a.m. Pratul Sharma has been riding his motor cycle bearing Reg. No.WB-38-AY-8802 along with pillion rider slowly, carefully, observing the traffic rules at Doddaballapur Junction, Devanahalli, Bengaluru District, at that time, a Toyota Qualis Car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-Z-4704 being driven by its driver at high speed in rash and negligent manner, all of a sudden entered highway without observing ongoing vehicles and dashed against his motor cycle, due to the terrific impact, PratulSharma and pillion rider fell down and sustained severe head and bodily SCCH 5 injuries and motor cycle was also badly damaged.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Akash Hospital, wherein duty Doctors have declared that, he was died on the way to the hospital.

Mahendra Kumar Sharma vs Rajkumar.M on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50194787/
2 3.

At the time of accident, deceased/Pratul Sharma was aged about 26 years, he was working as Assistant Material Manager at Rail Wheel Factory, Yelahanka, Bengaluru, thereby drawing a salary of Rs.1,00,000/- p.m.
petitioner No.1 is father and petitioner No.2 is mother of the deceased.
The deceased was a graduate of B.Tech and Civil Engineering and had SCCH 5 better future prospects with promotions, higher salary and other perks in his future life.
Due to sudden and untimely demise of the deceased, petitioners are undergoing great mental shock, agony and they have lost only bread earner of the family.
Out of the said accident, crime No.120/2022 is registered against the driver of Toyota Car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-Z-4704 before the Devanahalli Traffic police.
Respondent No.1 is the owner, respondent No.2 is insurer of the said offending car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

So that, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.4,00,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.

Further denied that alleged accident was occurred due to negligence of driver of the Toyota Qualis Car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-Z-4704.
SCCH 5

Further submitted that, said vehicle is insured with respondent No.2 vide its policy No.0731003121P105251589 valid from 01.09.2021 to 31.08.2022 and driver of the said vehicle had valid and effective driving licence vide No.KA0420030300672 VALID TILL 26.01.2032 and he is authorized to drive LMV and MCWG.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Respondent No.2/insurer insurer has appeared through counsel and filed written statement.
Respondent No.2 denied age, occupation, income of the deceased.

Further submitted that, alleged accident was occurred not only due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the Toyota Qualis Car but also negligency of motorist i.e., deceased Pratul Sharma, as such it is necessary to implead owner and insurer of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.WB-38-AY-8802 as necessary SCCH 5 parties for proper adjudication of the case.
Compensation claimed by the petitioners is on higher side.

Further admitted issuance of insurance policy bearing No.0731003121P105251589 valid for the period from 01.09.2021 to 31.08.2022 and liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further submitted that, driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-04- Z-4704 was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

Whether petitioners prove that, deceased Pratul Sharma died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 21.08.2022 at about 3.55 a.m. near Doddaballapura Junction, SCCH 5 Devanahalli, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent driving of Toyota Qualis Car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-Z-4704 dashed against deceased motor cycle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?

3
2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

7. In order to prove their case, Petitioner No.1/father of the deceased himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, further Assistant Personnel Office of Rail Wheel Factory is examined as PW-2, one eyewitness by name Rajiv Kumar Shaw is examined as PW-3 and marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.25 and closed his evidence.
Per contra, respondent No.l being the owner of the offending vehicle is examined as RW-1 and closed his evidence.
SCCH 5 8.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1/father of the deceased has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief-examination he has reiterated the facts narrated in their petition.

In this regard he has exhibited copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2,
copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of MVI Report is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of inquest is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of P.M. Report is SCCH 5 marked as Ex.P.7 and copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.8.
10 . Further one eyewitness i.e., pillion rider on the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.WB-38-AY-8802 being ridden by the deceased Pratul Sharma has deposed his evidence as PW-3.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1, PW-3 and the records those were marked i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar,
sketch, MVI Report, Inquest, P.M.Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioners about causing of the accident dated 21.08.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
11.
Per contra, respondent No.1/owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-Z-4704 has deposed his evidence as RW-1.

Further except oral evidence of respondent No.1, they have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non- causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and SCCH 5 evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioners about death of Pratul Sharma out of the accident held on 21.08.2022 at about 3.55 a.m. when he was riding motor cycle bearing Reg. No.WB-38-AY-8802 at Doddaballapur Junction, Devanahalli, Bengaluru District.

In the absence of iota of evidence, the Mahendra Kumar Sharma vs Rajkumar.M on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50194787/
4 arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioners.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioners, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
petitioners have proved the above issue No.1 in their favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
SCCH 5 13. Issue No.2:-
As per the case of the petitioners, deceased/Pratul Sharma was aged about 26 years as on the date of accident.

For proof of age of the deceased, they have produced copy of aadhar card of the deceased marked as Ex.P.11, wherein date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 25.03.1996, the alleged accident was occurred on 21.08.2022.

Accordingly relying on Ex.P.11, age of the deceased is considered about 27 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 17 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

In this regard they have exhibited school records marked as Ex.P.14, appointment letter SCCH 5 marked as Ex.P.15, copy of joining report is marked as Ex.P.16, payslips marked as Ex.P.17, copy of IT Returns for the year 2022-23 is marked as Ex.P.18.
15.

To prove their case, petitioners have examined Assistant Personnel Officer, Rail Wheel Factory,
Yelahanka, Bengaluru as PW-2, who exhibited authorization letter marked as Ex.P.20, copy of ID Card marked as Ex.P.21, copy of service card of the deceased as Ex.P.22, copy of payslips for the month of June and July 2022 is marked as Ex.P.23, supplementary bill for the month of August 2022 is marked as Ex.P.24 and full and final settlement letter is marked as Ex.P.25.
16. Further on perusal of Ex.P.16 joining report issued in favour of Pratul Sharma, Ex.P.17 payslips,
Ex.P.18 IT returns, Ex.P.20 payslips issued by Rail Wheel Factory and Ex.P.23 are payslips and on perusal of evidence of RW-1 and charge sheet it clearly indicates to SCCH 5 the court that, charge sheet has been filed against respondent No.1.

So on perusal of Ex.P.16, Ex.P.18, Ex.P.23 and other documents including IT returns filed by the deceased Pratul Sharma clearly indicates to the court that, he was earning definite income of Rs.64,896/- for the month of May 2022, Rs.63,321/- for the month of June 2022, Rs.69,127/- for the month of July 2022 as net salary, that means, prior to the accident deceased Pratul Sharma was earning Rs.69,127/-p.m.
So for the future prospects, the said salary is taken into consideration as notional income of the deceased Pratul Sharm.
Further IT returns marked as Ex.P.18 submitted by the petitioners is with regard to income of deceased Pratul Sharma.
Accordingly notional income of the deceased is taken at the rate of Rs.69,127/- p.m. for the purpose of calculation of loss of dependency.

Further petitioner No.1 is father and petitioner No.2 is mother of the deceased/Pratul Sharma.

To prove the said facts, they have furnished notarized copy of aadhar card of petitioner No.1 and 2 marked as Ex.P.19 it reveals that, they are legal representatives of the deceased/Pratul Sharma,
hence they will become dependents of the deceased.
18.

As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the deceased is bachelor, then 1/2 of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/2 of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

19. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, the Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, an addition of 40% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged below 40 years, in case SCCH 5 of fixed salary employee.

In the said rulings their lordships have held the following principles;
a) Merely in the alleged accident two or more vehicles are involved, then claimants shall be liable for compensation only from the Insurance Company and SCCH 5 merely some of the parties have not been included is not a sole ground to decline the relief Mahendra Kumar Sharma vs Rajkumar.

7 b) If the owner and driver of the offending vehicle have not contested the case and Insurance Company has not adduced evidence, then Insurance Company is liable to pay compensation and principles of contributory negligence is not attracts.
c) If the tribunals have passed award against both owner and insurer, then claimant is entitled for award against both of them.

d) If there is no direct evidence by the Insurance Company with regard to contributory negligence of the deceased in the alleged accident, then the tribunals have no jurisdiction to impose as well as apply principles of contributory negligence for any extent.
SCCH 5 e) The burden lies on the Insurance Company to prove the principles of negligence on the part of the deceased.

f) The tribunals should take notional income of the deceased in average manner if the party has placed payslips etc.
26.

So as per the ratios of petitioners rulings, respondent No.2 Insurance Company has not proved the negligency on the part of the deceased Pratul Sharma and also on respondent No.1, because except filing of written statement and cross-examination of witness, respondent No.2 has not adduced any evidence to substantiate written statement contents.

So in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioners and rulings submitted by the petitioners and respondent No.2 alone is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners and further as SCCH 5 stated above, notional income of the deceased Pratul Sharma is considered as stated above.

27. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer of the Toyota Qualis Car bearing Reg.
No.KA-04- Z-4704 has issued insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 vide policy bearing No.0731003121P105251589 which is valid from 01.09.2021 to 31.08.2022, the alleged accident was occurred on 21.08.2022, hence as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

So that,
respondent No.2/insurer of the Toyota Qualis Car is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
SCCH 5 28. Issue No.3:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:

The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.99,41,356/- (Rupees Ninety Nine Lakhs Forty One Thousand Three Hundred Fifty Six Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio 50:50 in the award amount.

The petitioners are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in SCCH 5 any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
